g.text: DESIGN ONE-PAGER · HOLD AND PICKUP SERVICE
Library holds, from the catalogue to the pickup shelf
A patron places a hold in the catalogue app. The service keeps a line of holds for each title, sets a returned copy aside at the patron's branch, and tells the patron it is ready to collect.
Branch staff track holds on paper slips and by phone. A patron has to call or visit a branch to place one.
Patrons need to place a hold online, keep their place in line, and hear when a copy is ready to collect.
Accept a hold placed in the catalogue app and show the patron their place in line.
Set each returned copy aside for the first confirmed hold on its title.
Tell the patron by email or text when the copy is ready, with a collect-by date.
Release a copy nobody collects in seven days to the next hold in line.
Interlibrary loans: the service fills holds with copies this library owns.
Place hold: takes the card, the title and the branch, returns the hold.
Cancel hold: releases the hold and its place in line.
List holds: filters by card, title and branch.
Copy check-in event: carries the copy and the branch that received it.
A notice sent to an old address or number leaves the copy unclaimed. A bounced notice flags the card for the desk, and
the copy still expires after seven days.
Decision: queue between API and worker
Pickup runs asynchronously. The API returns once the hold is queued, so a busy branch never holds a patron's request
Place a hold: title, pickup branch, notice channel, confirm
Hold shelf: title, library card, slot, collect-by date
The numbered links follow one hold from the catalogue app to the holds store.
